what_works: Geopolitical power rankings and Indian pride themes consistently break 2,000 to 3,500 views (e.g., 'India's Highest-Earning Cities', 'दुनिया के Top 5 सबसे Powerful देश!').
Hindi or bilingual titles with dramatic emojis (😱, 🇮🇳, 🚀, 🔥) dominate the channel's top quintile.
Morning publication window between 06:00 and 09:00 IST correlates with the majority of top-tier videos (3,516, 3,330, 2,617, and 2,313 views were all published 06:00-09:00 IST).
Listicle formats and comparative showdowns ('Top 5', 'US vs North Korea', 'India-China') drive the highest view counts and comment rates.
Videos with custom thumbnails consistently hit the channel median or above, whereas non-thumbnailed recent uploads largely flopped below 100 views.

diagnosis.hook: The top videos hook viewers using high-stakes curiosity or national relevance ('भारत किस नंबर पर है?', 'India's Highest-Earning Cities'), whereas the bottom videos open with dry academic titles ('Photosynthesis Explained') or obscure foreign history that gives the Hindi viewer zero reason not to swipe away in the first 2 seconds.
diagnosis.buildup: High performers use comparative progression (rankings 5 to 1, or nation vs. nation tension) which naturally sustains retention. The bottom videos appear to be linear informational monologues that plateau quickly.
diagnosis.visuals: The winning cluster overwhelmingly features active custom thumbnails and vibrant, identifiable national flags/symbols. The bottom 8 videos either skipped custom thumbnails entirely or relied on auto-selected frames of mud walls, shrimp, and concrete.
diagnosis.titles_topics: There is a severe audience identity split: TruFact was built on Hindi/Hinglish geopolitical, military, and Indian economic curiosities. Recent uploads abruptly pivoted to English-titled biology lectures and Western/Asian ancient history, alienating the channel's core audience segment.
diagnosis.other: Sample size caution: Some weak videos ('Battle of Myeongnyang', 'Sacred Cats') are under 3 days old, so their total numbers are not fully matured; however, their initial trajectory (under 20 views) proves that the algorithm found zero swipe-through interest from TruFact's subscriber base.

hook_rules: Ask a direct question that challenges common knowledge in the first 2 seconds (e.g., 'क्या आप जानते हैं...?').
Anchor the hook to India or a globally recognizable superpower (India, USA, China, Russia) within the first frame.
Show a high-contrast visual shock or animated stat counter immediately on screen 0:00 to stop scrolling.
State the high-stakes outcome first, then promise the reveal at the end ('दुनिया का सबसे खतरनाक हथियार किसके पास है?').
Avoid slow channel introductions, logos, greetings, or text cards that take more than 0.5 seconds.
buildup_rules: Use the countdown/rankings structure (e.g., Number 5 to Number 1) to build innate suspense.
Cut and transition visual assets every 1.5 to 2.5 seconds to maintain high visual pacing.
Incorporate rising background audio tension or rhythmic sound effects on every data point reveal.
Place the biggest reveal or plot twist at second 40+ to maximize completion rate and looped replays.
visual_rules: Always set a custom thumbnail frame featuring large high-contrast Hindi text (maximum 3 words) and an emotional face or recognized flag.
Use bold, dual-colored subtitles (e.g., Yellow and White text with black stroke) centered in the readable Shorts safe zone.
Avoid static Wikipedia or Google images; use Ken Burns zoom pans, motion graphics, or map animations.
Color-grade clips with high saturation and contrast so they stand out in mobile feeds under varying brightness.
title_rules: Write titles in Devnagari Hindi or mixed Hinglish—never 100% formal academic English on this channel.
Include at least one high-emotion emoji (😱, 🔥, 🇮🇳, ⚠️) to trigger immediate cognitive curiosity.
Keep titles under 55 characters so the punchline does not get truncated on mobile screens.
Double-check title metadata before publishing to prevent accidental copy-paste tags like 'Description:'.
topic_rules: Stick strictly to the core content pillars: Indian geopolitics, military defense, mega-infrastructure, and astonishing world records.
Filter every idea through the 'Dinner Table Test': Would an average Indian viewer share this fact with friends or family?
Avoid standard school-syllabus science topics (e.g., photosynthesis, cell division) unless framed as a bizarre conspiracy, mystery, or survival story.
avoid: Academic lecture titles ('Photosynthesis Explained', 'The Architecture of...').
Obscure foreign history with unpronounceable names ('Myeongnyang') with zero connection to Indian viewers.
Publishing without a verified custom thumbnail.
Pure English titles that alienate your primary Hindi Shorts recommendation feed.
Copy-pasting description text into title fields without proofreading.
Posting saturated facts without a contrarian or fresh angle.
